title: The Dynamic Theory of Economic Complexity
abstract: arXiv:2512.10672v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Why do some activities grow faster in some economies than others? We develop a dynamic model of economic complexity in which output is determined by a weak-link production function and investment contributes to the accumulation of capabilities shared across activities. We test the model empirically by exploring two of its predictions. First, the model predicts that the capability stock at which the accumulation of a capability is fastest increases with the capability requirements of an activity. This implies a transition from unconditional to conditional convergence and a tunable conditional convergence regime. Second, shared capabilities provide a mechanism for path-dependent diversification (the principle of relatedness), including signs for the expected interaction terms between relatedness and complexity terms in regressions exploring growth by economy and activity. translated_title: 经济复杂性的动态理论
translated_abstract: 为什么有些活动在某些经济体中比在其他经济体增长得更快？我们建立了一个经济复杂性的动态模型，其中产出由弱连接生产函数决定，而投资有助于积累跨活动共享的能力。我们通过检验该模型的两个预测来进行实证验证。首先，模型预测能力积累速度最快时所对应的能力存量会随着某项活动的能力需求而增加，这意味着经济从无条件收敛向条件收敛的转变，并形成一个可调节的条件收敛机制。其次，共享能力为路径依赖的多样化（即相关性原理）提供了一种机制，包括在探索经济体与活动增长的回归分析中，相关性与复杂性交互项的预期符号。我们利用国际贸易数据及相关数据对这些预测进行了评估。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于弱连接生产函数与跨活动共享能力积累的经济复杂性动态理论，预测了从无条件收敛到可调节条件收敛的转变以及路径依赖多样化机制，并通过国际贸易数据进行了实证检验。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a dynamic theory of economic complexity based on weak-link production and shared capability accumulation, predicting a transition from unconditional to tunable conditional convergence and a mechanism for path-dependent diversification, empirically validated using international trade data.
